title: Returns credit check for independent bookshops

fixture.label: queue #11 benchmark: a fictional opportunity written for the benchmark; every fact, source and value in it is test data

upstream_status.summary: Fictional benchmark opportunity: no upstream screening was run (test data).

buyer: Owner-managers of independent bookshops with 1-3 staff, members of the (fictional) Northvale Booksellers Guild
user: The shop's owner-manager, who does the returns paperwork
job: Each month, match the books the shop returned to publishers and distributors against the credit notes they send back, find missing or short credits, and send each supplier a query listing them.

evidence.claim: Guild member survey (fictional, 2026, 112 of 340 member shops answered): 71% reconcile returns credits by hand, a median of 5 hours a month.
evidence.quote: 71% of responding shops reconcile returns credits by hand, a median of 5 hours a month
evidence.source: Northvale Booksellers Guild member survey 2026 (fictional test document)

evidence.claim: Interviews with six owner-managers (fictional, September 2026): five had found at least one missing or short credit in the last quarter; the median amount missing was $180.
evidence.quote: Five of the six owner-managers had found at least one missing or short credit in the last quarter; the median amount missing was $180
evidence.source: Queue #11 interview notes, six owner-managers (fictional test document)

evidence.claim: An owner-manager describes the manual check (fictional interview).
evidence.quote: I print the returns list and the credit notes and tick them off with a pen. It takes most of a Sunday.
evidence.source: Queue #11 interview notes, six owner-managers (fictional test document)

evidence.claim: Owner-managers want to approve any query before it goes to a supplier (fictional interview).
evidence.quote: I want to see what it's going to say to the rep before anything goes out
evidence.source: Queue #11 interview notes, six owner-managers (fictional test document)

evidence.claim: The two largest distributors offer credit notes as CSV downloads with a documented column layout (fictional).
evidence.quote: Credit notes are available as CSV with the columns ISBN, quantity, unit credit, returns authorisation number

evidence.claim: The shops' point-of-sale systems export returns lists as CSV (fictional).
evidence.quote: Export returns as CSV: ISBN, title, quantity, supplier, returns authorisation number

evidence.claim: The guild's software list has no tool that matches returns to credit notes (fictional).
evidence.quote: None of the listed systems matches returns to credit notes
evidence.source: Northvale Booksellers Guild software list (fictional test document)

open_unknowns.question: Do smaller publishers send credit notes only as PDF, which would need manual entry?
Will shops beyond the ones interviewed pay the target price?
How often do the distributors change their CSV layout?

appetite.note: Test fixture for the queue #11 benchmark: not an owner commitment.

constraints.text: No contact with real shops, suppliers or anyone else: this is a fictional benchmark case.
The owner-manager approves every supplier query before it is sent; the tool never sends anything itself.
Works from CSV files the shop downloads; no integration with point-of-sale or distributor systems in the first version.

proposed_solution.summary: Upload the month's returns CSV and the distributors' credit-note CSVs; the tool matches lines by returns authorisation number and ISBN, lists missing and short credits, and drafts one query per supplier for the owner-manager to edit and approve before sending it from their own email.

features.name: CSV upload and matching
features.does: Match returns lines to credit-note lines by returns authorisation number and ISBN

features.name: Mismatch list
features.does: List missing and short credits per supplier, with amounts

features.name: Query drafts for approval
features.does: Draft one query per supplier listing its mismatches; the owner-manager edits, approves and sends it from their own email

success_bar.value: At least 4 of 6 pilot shops finish a month's returns check with the tool in under half the time they report today, and each finds or rules out missing credits, within 6 weeks of starting
